title_as_printed: Solubility of nitrogen in aqueous calcium chloride, and in a solution both 1.5 N in NaCl and 5.41 N in CaCl2, at 30°C

composition.other_species: mixed salt block: NaCl and CaCl2 both set by the label row
composition.note: Composition is set per block by the label rows (group_rows), unit N = equivalents per litre of solution.

skip_rows.reason: block label row giving the concentration of the rows below (also repeated column header absent: header printed once per block pair)

conversion_needs: Concentration is normality (equivalents/L of solution), not molality: N = mol/L x charge equivalents (for CaCl2, Na2SO4, MgSO4 1 N = 0.5 mol/L; for NaCl 1 N = 1 mol/L). Conversion to mol/kg needs solution density at 30 C, which the paper does not give.
Mole fraction of N2 is printed x10^4: stored value must be multiplied by 1e-4. Basis (mole fraction in the whole liquid, salt as undissociated species or ions) is not stated.
Pressure psia to MPa (x 0.00689476); pressure is total pressure with no correction for water vapour (stated for water, Table 2 text), whether this holds for the salt solutions is not stated.
Temperature given only as 30 C (303.15 K); temperature scale not stated.
notes: Table printed as side-by-side blocks; stacked here one block after another with the printed block heading as a label row. Printed table title says '1.5 N in NaCl' but the block heading and the text both say 1.38 N; the block heading (1.38 N) is used. 11.19 N CaCl2 (about 5.6 mol/L) may be near or beyond CaCl2 solubility at 30 C; flagged for the builder, not judged here. The 1.38 N NaCl + 5.41 N CaCl2 block is a mixed-salt block.
